Around 3,000 protesters from Akbayan Partylist, civil society coalition Tindig Pilipinas, the Nagkaisa labor coalition, ML Partylist, Kalipunan, youth and student organizations, and grassroots communities marched to the gates of the Senate today with one clear demand: Convene the impeachment court now. Try Vice President Sara Duterte.

Akbayan, which endorsed the first impeachment complaint, pointed to the growing national clamor for an impeachment trial. “This is no longer just an opposition campaign,” said Akbayan Party President Rafaela David. “More and more people are stepping forward because the Senate refuses to. Universities, law schools, religious denominations, legal and constitutional luminaries, business leaders, and trade unions — lahat malinaw ang panawagan. The only obstacle is the Senate leadership, who seem either afraid or determined to protect the impeached Vice President.”

David challenged the Senate leadership to act with courage. “Sa lahat ng uri ng keso, si Senate President Chiz na lang yata ang ayaw matunaw sa init ng katotohanan. Panahon na para makinig sila sa tinig ng mamamayan at magpakita ng lakas ng loob. Tama na ang mga palusot. Sundin ang Konstitusyon. Litisin si impeached Vice President Sara Duterte.”

Akbayan also slammed Senate Majority Leader Francis Tolentino’s proposal to limit the impeachment trial to a 19-day package within the 19th Congress, calling it “absurd” and “a trap disguised as compromise.”

“Dinelay nila ang proseso, ngayon gusto nila tayong pagmamadaliin? Anong kalokohan ito? Senator Tolentino’s proposal is a pathetic attempt to save face after his widely mocked ‘de facto dismissal’ argument. It’s also a demolition job in disguise,” David said. 

“Senator Tolentino’s proposal clearly undermines the prosecution’s right to present its case within a reasonable period and hold a proper pre-trial. Also, his suggestion to select only two articles of impeachment is like asking the aggrieved to pick just their top two traumas—for the Senate’s convenience. Let’s make this clear to Senator Tolentino: the impeachment court is not a fast-food drive-thru,” David asserted.

The protest march began at the Manila Film Center and concluded at the Senate gates with a multi-faith ecumenical gathering. Organizers also announced a candlelight vigil on Tuesday evening, and a Day of Action for Truth and Accountability on Wednesday, as the Senate is expected to deliberate on the impeachment case.

#AkbayanPartylist

THOUSANDS MARCH TO SENATE, URGE START OF IMPEACHMENT TRIAL VS SARA DUTERTE

LOOK: Around 3,000 protesters from Akbayan Partylist, Tindig Pilipinas, the Nagkaisa labor coalition, ML Partylist, Kalipunan, youth and student groups, and grassroots communities marched to the Senate gates on Monday, calling on senators to convene the impeachment court and begin the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Carrying banners "Sundin ang Konstitusyon" and "Impeachment Trial Ngayon," the demonstrators joined a protest march dubbed Forthwith March, which began at the Manila Film Center and ended at the Senate. The rally concluded with a multi-faith ecumenical gathering.

Akbayan Party President Rafaela David said the call for an impeachment trial is no longer limited to opposition groups. "More and more people are stepping forward because the Senate refuses to. Universities, law schools, religious denominations, legal and constitutional luminaries, business leaders, and trade unions — lahat malinaw ang panawagan," she said.

David criticized Senate President Chiz Escudero for allegedly stonewalling the trial: "Sa lahat ng uri ng keso, si Senate President Chiz na lang yata ang ayaw matunaw sa init ng katotohanan."

She also slammed outgoing Senate Majority Leader Francis Tolentino's proposal to compress the trial into 19 session days, calling it "absurd" and "a trap disguised as compromise."

"Dinelay nila ang proseso, ngayon gusto nila tayong pagmadaliin? Anong kalokohan ito?" David said, adding that the suggestion to reduce the Articles of Impeachment from seven to two undermines the prosecution’s right to present its case.

"The impeachment court is not a fast-food drive-thru," she said.

Organizers announced a candlelight vigil at the Senate on Tuesday evening and a "Day of Action for Truth and Accountability" on Wednesday, coinciding with the Senate's expected deliberations on the impeachment case.

📷 Tindig Pilipinas, Akbayan Partylist
